questions.context: En una finca de Fusagasugá, Mariana escucha a un animal rosado que come en el barro.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A dog says "woof, woof", not "oink".
Incorrect. A fish lives in water and makes no "oink" sound.
Incorrect. A hen says "cluck, cluck", a different sound from "oink".
Correct. The pig is the pink farm animal that says "oink, oink".

questions.explanation: En inglés los animales hacen sonidos distintos a los del español. El cerdo o marrano se dice "pig" y su sonido es "oink, oink". El perro dice "woof" y la gallina dice "cluck".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: En un apartamento de Cali, Sebastián tiene una pecera con una mascota de color naranja.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A cat lives on land and does not like to get wet.
Correct. A fish lives in water and swims in a fish tank or a river.
Incorrect. A horse is a big farm animal that walks and runs on land, not in water.
Incorrect. A pig lives on a farm, on land, and does not live in water.

questions.explanation: "Fish" significa pez. Los peces viven en el agua y pueden ser mascotas en una pecera. El gato ("cat"), el caballo ("horse") y el cerdo ("pig") viven en la tierra.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: En la finca de su abuela en Santander, Juan recoge los huevos del gallinero para el desayuno.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A cow gives us milk, not eggs.
Incorrect. A horse helps on the farm and people ride it, but it does not lay eggs.
Correct. A hen is a female chicken, and hens lay the eggs we eat.
Incorrect. A dog is a pet that plays and guards the house, and it does not lay eggs.

questions.explanation: "Hen" significa gallina. Las gallinas ponen los huevos ("eggs") que comemos en el desayuno, por ejemplo en los huevos pericos. También se puede decir "chicken" para el ave en general.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "A ______ has wool. We make ruanas and sweaters with it."
questions.context: En Nariño, la abuela de Camila teje una ruana con la lana de los animales de su finca.

options.feedback: Correct. A sheep has soft white wool, and people use it to make ruanas and sweaters.
Incorrect. A fish has scales and lives in water, so it has no wool.
Incorrect. A hen has feathers and gives eggs, not wool.
Incorrect. A cat has fur, but we do not make sweaters from a pet cat.

questions.explanation: "Sheep" significa oveja. La oveja tiene lana ("wool") y con ella se tejen ruanas y sacos, como en Boyacá y Nariño. Ojo: "sheep" es igual en singular y plural: "one sheep, two sheep".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Grandpa: "Let's ride on the farm!"
Ana: "Ride what?"
Grandpa: "The ______. It is big and it runs fast."
questions.context: Ana visita la finca de su abuelo en el Eje Cafetero y él le propone dar un paseo por las montañas.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A fish is small and lives in water, so nobody can ride it.
Incorrect. A hen is a small bird that gives eggs, too small for a person to ride.
Correct. A horse is big and fast, and people ride horses on farms.
Incorrect. A cat is a small pet, so a person cannot ride it.

questions.explanation: Las pistas son "ride" (montar), "big" (grande) y "runs fast" (corre rápido). El único animal grande y rápido que se puede montar es el caballo, que en inglés se dice "horse".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "On my grandpa's finca there are three cows, two pigs and five sheep. The cows give us milk."
How many pigs are there?
questions.context: Un niño de Duitama describe los animales de la finca de su abuelo en Boyacá.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says "three cows"; three is the number of cows, not pigs.
Incorrect. The number five goes with "sheep" in the text, not with pigs.
Incorrect. The word "one" does not appear next to any animal in the text.
Correct. The text says "two pigs", so there are 2 pigs on the finca.

questions.explanation: En el texto cada número va justo antes del animal: "three cows" (tres vacas), "two pigs" (dos cerdos) y "five sheep" (cinco ovejas). Para encontrar la respuesta hay que buscar el número que acompaña a "pigs", y es "two".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "I have a pet. It is small. It has four legs and a long tail. It says 'meow' and it likes milk."
What is the pet?
questions.context: En Neiva, Lucía escribe una adivinanza sobre su mascota para que sus compañeros la descubran.

options.feedback: Correct. A cat is small, has four legs and a long tail, and says "meow".
Incorrect. A dog also has four legs and a tail, but it says "woof", not "meow".
Incorrect. A bird has two legs and wings, so it does not match "four legs".
Incorrect. A pig says "oink", and its tail is short and curly, not long.

questions.explanation: Hay que usar todas las pistas. El perro también tiene cuatro patas y cola, pero la pista decisiva es el sonido: "meow" (miau) es el sonido del gato. Por eso la mascota es "a cat".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: En una clase de inglés en Sincelejo, los niños revisan oraciones sobre lo que nos dan los animales de la finca.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Sheep give us wool; eggs come from hens.
Correct. Cows give milk, which we drink and use to make cheese.
Incorrect. Horses do not lay eggs; we ride them and they carry things.
Incorrect. Fish have scales, not wool; wool comes from sheep.

questions.explanation: Cada animal de la finca nos da algo distinto: la vaca ("cow") da leche ("milk"), la gallina ("hen") da huevos ("eggs") y la oveja ("sheep") da lana ("wool"). Solo la oración "Cows give us milk" es verdadera.
questions.subject: ingles
